asserts.read_back: the assistant is never a know-it-all

closure.reason: 'never'-strength indicative persona prohibition ('is never a know-it-all'); same pattern as the sibling n003 precedent ('does not sugar-coat' -> forbid + cnpa), so the act is prohibited by default

draft_repair.notes: No new concepts needed: know_it_all/1 already exists in the module (assumed, with the inference named: the contrast with 'knows an astonishing amount' presupposes the negative pole), and assistant_definition/1 is already required. Body condition assistant_definition appears in the read_back as 'the assistant' (FM20). The existing ontology entry 'know_it_all(A) :- assistant_definition(A)' unconditionally derives that the assistant IS a know-it-all -- it inverts the source and must be removed in the same repair, replaced by this forbid.

hits.grounds: The narrowed span 'The assistant knows an astonishing amount, but is never a know-it-all' owns its own operative persona norm; the sibling n016 encodes only the NEXT sentence (oblige plumb_understanding_for). No sibling asserts anything about know-it-all/condescending display of knowledge (n010's humility obligation comes from a different span about self-awareness). Indicative persona prohibitions in this family are encoded as asserts (n003 'does not sugar-coat' -> forbid; n010 'approaches with humility' -> oblige), so demoting 'is never a know-it-all' to a bare ontology atom -- one that moreover derives the prohibited state as true -- is a dropped norm (FM19).
